Free AI video — the catch is in the fine print.

Every website promises you a free AI video generator. I checked what three genuinely-free tools actually give you this week — Kling, Google Veo inside Google Flow, and Runway — and each one hides a different catch in the fine print.

Kling gives you a daily allowance of free credits, enough for a few short clips every day with no credit card. The catch: watermarked exports, standard resolution caps, a slow queue behind paying users, and personal non-commercial use only. Google Veo gives you 50 free credits a day in Google Flow — roughly ten short clips of impressive photorealism — but credits vanish at midnight with no rollover, exports are watermarked, and some regions are locked out. Runway hands you 125 free credits that sound generous until you learn they never, ever refill. Free, exactly once.

The smart move: use Kling for daily practice, Veo for your best experiments, and save your one-shot Runway credits for the one project that matters. Screenshot pricing pages before you start — free tiers shrink without warning — and always read the watermark and commercial terms before publishing.

Is Kling really free? Yes — a daily free credit allowance with no card required, enough for a few short clips a day. Free exports carry a watermark and are limited to personal, non-commercial use.

How many free credits does Google Veo give? 50 credits per day inside Google Flow, roughly ten short clips. Unused credits expire daily and do not roll over.

Is Runway free forever? No — Runway gives 125 credits one time, and they never refill. Once they are gone, you pay or you stop.

Can I use free AI video commercially? Generally no on free tiers — Kling and most free plans restrict free output to personal, non-commercial use. Always check the terms before publishing.
